units.oneLiner: Keep every key in the slot array itself and, when the home slot is taken, probe the next slot and the next: the probes stay inside the cache line the first one fetched, Knuth's 1963 formulas say exactly what each load factor costs, and the price is clustering, which is why the table resizes before it is full and why the hash must scatter neighbors.
units.description: Linear probing on 65,536 slots against Knuth's 1963 formulas (within 1% to load 0.7) and a Python set over 1,200,000 operations: at load 0.9 a hit costs 5.315 probes but 1.540 cache lines against 2.570 and 2.570 for double hashing; clusters of 715 slots; tombstones 5.864 probes per miss against 1.698 for backward shift; a weak hash costs 1,056 probes per hit.
units.time: O(1) expected; (1 + 1/(1 - a)) / 2 probes per hit

units.plan_row: Open addressing × Linear probing. Puzzle 172, data-structures (problemSlug hash-collision-resolution, the atlas problem page carrying "Cache-friendly hashing"; sibling live lesson cuckoo-hashing-two-table-eviction-kicks). Solution open_addressing_linear_probing.py (3.0s, prints OK): linear probing with tombstone or backward-shift deletion and a rebuild at 85% live-plus-tombstones, quadratic probing (triangular offsets), double hashing (odd stride), separate chaining, Robin Hood, Fibonacci and weak hashes, a probe-and-cache-line counter (8 slots per 64-byte line, one line per chaining node). ORACLES: (1) Knuth 1963 at loads 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.7 / 0.8 / 0.9 / 0.95: hits 1.164 / 1.509 / 2.172 / 3.027 / 5.962 / 11.609 against 1.167 / 1.500 / 2.167 / 3.000 / 5.500 / 10.500, misses 1.397 / 2.510 / 5.971 / 12.655 / 50.434 / 205.639 against 1.389 / 2.500 / 6.056 / 13.000 / 50.500 / 200.500 (within 6% to 0.8, 20% beyond); (2) 1,200,000 mixed operations across six structures all matching a Python set, final sizes matching; (3) the race at load 0.9 (every key looked up, 5,000 misses): linear probing 5.315 probes/hit, 47.975/miss, 1.540 lines/hit, variance 277, max 612, longest cluster 715; Robin Hood 5.315 / 5.644 / 1.540 / 19.8 / 29; quadratic 2.850 / 12.055 / 1.951 / 16.2 / 92; double hashing 2.570 / 10.056 / 2.570 / 11.1 / 68; chaining 2.450 / 1.923 / 2.450 / 0.5 / 9; longest run by load 8 / 31 / 85 / 209 / 752 / 3,250; (4) deletion: fill to 0.7, delete half: tombstones 5.864 probes per miss (formula for 0.7: 6.056), backward shift 1.698 (formula for 0.35: 1.683); (5) weak hash (high bits) on 2,048 consecutive keys in 4,096 slots: linear probing 1,056 probes per hit, double hashing 8.3, chaining 402.8, strong hash 1.50. Honest: linear probing pays twice double hashing's probes at 0.9 and wins only on lines; the Robin Hood mean is identical to 1e-9 (the displacement total is invariant), asserted; three author notes recorded (quadratic vs double ordering; the first weak-hash experiment at 65,536 slots ran quadratic for ten minutes and was shrunk; a 5,000-key hit sample was replaced by every key after the early-inserted keys biased it). Cards: self, Hash table with chaining, Robin Hood hashing, Cuckoo hashing (live lesson badge) (all algoName). neverUse: linear probing with a hash that keeps neighbors neighbors. Figure: Knuth's hit and miss curves with the measured points beside bars of the longest run by load; cite Knuth 1963 / TAOCP 3 6.4, Amdahl et al. 1954, Pagh-Pagh-Ruzic STOC 2007 DOI 10.1145/1250790.1250839. Viz LinearProbingViz: a 64-slot table as eight cache lines filling to load 0.9, walked slots amber and touched lines outlined, the running average probes per insert against Knuth's expectation, every key checked reachable from its home each tick; NODE-VERIFIED 20 cycles x 21 ticks, 0 breaks; stepMs 500, holdTicks rests. Preserved narration: Aoede + Algieba.

units.oneLiner: Model the number in the system as a chain that climbs at the arrival rate and falls at the service rate, cut it between every two neighboring states and equate the flows, and the whole distribution is geometric, each extra customer rho times as likely as the last: L = rho / (1 - rho), W = 1 / (mu - lambda), P(wait) = rho, with Little's law for free and the same recursion for any number of servers.
units.description: M/M/1 by the birth-death balance equations against a discrete-event simulation at six utilizations: the closed form reproduced to 3e-11 and the simulation within three standard errors of L, Wq, P(wait), and P(N >= 5); L runs 1, 4, 9, 19, 99 at rho 0.5 to 0.99; M/D/1 halves the queue wait (4.50 against 9.00 at rho 0.9); capacity reasoning predicts no wait where the measured wait is 8.4 service times.
units.time: O(1) per measure in closed form; O(states) for the numerical chain
units.plan_row: M/M/1 analysis × Birth-death balance equations. Puzzle 176, probabilistic (problemSlug queueing-performance, the atlas problem page carrying "Single-queue analysis"; sibling live lesson discrete-event-simulation-event-queue-advance, puzzle 136). Solution mm1_analysis_birth_death_balance_equations.py (0.6s, prints OK): a birth-death solver (recursion and normalization on a truncated chain with any death-rate function), measures from a distribution, the M/M/1 and M/D/1 (Pollaczek-Khinchine) closed forms, Kingman's G/G/1 approximation, and an event-list discrete-event simulation (one or more servers, exponential or fixed service, warm-up, batch-means standard errors). ORACLES (mu = 1): (1) the numerical chain against the closed form, worst disagreement 2.7e-11 over L, Lq, W, Wq, P(wait) at seven utilizations; Little's law and pi_n geometric to 1e-9; (2) the simulation, rho / L formula / L sim (se) / Wq formula / Wq sim (se) / P(wait) formula, sim / P(N >= 5) formula, sim / events: 0.30 0.429 0.430 (0.004) 0.429 0.437 (0.009) 0.300 0.302 0.002 0.003 120,000; 0.50 1.000 1.018 (0.012) 1.000 1.039 (0.019) 0.500 0.506 0.031 0.033 120,000; 0.70 2.333 2.323 (0.072) 2.333 2.347 (0.091) 0.700 0.697 0.168 0.164 120,000; 0.80 4.000 3.948 (0.132) 4.000 3.962 (0.155) 0.800 0.793 0.328 0.320 120,000; 0.90 9.000 8.466 (0.338) 9.000 8.428 (0.370) 0.900 0.897 0.590 0.571 240,000; 0.95 19.000 17.039 (1.049) 19.000 16.960 (1.078) 0.950 0.950 0.774 0.770 240,000; Little's law inside the run within 8%; (3) rivals at rho 0.8 / 0.9: M/D/1 Wq 2.000 / 4.500 (simulated 2.020 +/- 0.042 / 4.497 +/- 0.319), W 3.000 / 5.500; M/M/2 with two half-speed servers (death rate min(n, 2) mu / 2) L 4.444 / 9.474 (simulated 4.342 +/- 0.187 / 9.206 +/- 0.491), W 5.556 / 10.526, Wq 3.556 / 8.526; Kingman with ca2 = cs2 = 1 exact (4.000 / 9.000) and exact for M/D/1 with cs2 = 0; (4) L = 1, 4, 9, 19, 99 at rho 0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99; (5) capacity reasoning predicts Wq 0 against simulated 8.43 service times at rho 0.9 (P(N >= 5) 0.57) and 16.96 at 0.95. Honest: the rho 0.95 simulation sits two standard errors under 19 after 120,000 customers (slow relaxation near saturation) and the page says so; author correction recorded (short batches gave correlated means at high utilization, longer batches used and reported). Cards: self, Pollaczek-Khinchine formula, Erlang C formula, Discrete event simulation (live lesson badge) (all algoName). neverUse: capacity reasoning, lambda < mu so nobody waits. Figure: geometric state probabilities at rho 0.5 and 0.9 beside L against rho on a log scale with the simulated points and three-sigma bars; cite Erlang 1909, Kendall 1953 DOI 10.1214/aoms/1177728975, Little 1961. Viz Mm1Viz: a live M/M/1 lane at utilization 0.5 / 0.7 / 0.85 by cycle, 40 events per tick for 90 ticks, the share of time in each state as amber bars against the geometric law's blue ticks, the running time average against rho / (1 - rho), the count, the time shares summing to one, and Little's law checked every tick; NODE-VERIFIED 20 cycles x 90 ticks, 0 breaks; stepMs 160, holdTicks rests. units.oneLiner: Add Laplace noise with scale equal to the most one record can change the answer, divided by epsilon: the output densities for any two databases differing in one record then stay within a factor of e to the epsilon everywhere, which is the definition of differential privacy, and the price is a mean absolute error of exactly that scale, with budgets that add across releases.
units.description: The Laplace mechanism held to its guarantee: the output-density ratio on neighboring databases within e^epsilon in every populated bin, the exact ratio tight at 2.718; mean absolute error equal to the scale b at four epsilons; ten composed releases inside the composed epsilon; a membership attacker at 0.698 against the 0.731 bound, 1.000 against exact release and 0.952 against uncalibrated noise; Gaussian loses one count, wins a batch of fifty.
units.plan_row: Differential privacy × Laplace mechanism. Puzzle 177, crypto-number-theory (problemSlug differential-privacy, the atlas problem page carrying "Private data release"). Solution differential_privacy_laplace_mechanism.py (1.3s, prints OK): an inverse-transform Laplace sampler and density, a 1,000-record database (sensitive bit, bounded value) and its neighbor, count / sum / mean / median queries, a local-sensitivity scan over every record and both extreme replacements, the Gaussian scale formula, randomized response, and a two-database attacker. ORACLES: (1) the guarantee at epsilon 1: 200,000 releases per neighbor, 10 bins with 2,000+ draws, worst empirical ratio 2.785 vs e^epsilon 2.718 (inside the 10% margin), exact density ratio on a grid peaks at 2.718282 and never above; (2) utility at epsilon 0.1 / 0.5 / 1 / 2: MAE 9.994 / 1.986 / 1.004 / 0.503 vs b = 10 / 2 / 1 / 0.5, variance 199.21 / 7.89 / 2.00 / 0.51 vs 2 b^2 = 200 / 8 / 2 / 0.5; (3) sensitivity, measured vs global: count 1.000 / 1, sum 99.986 / 100, mean 0.100 / 0.100, median 0.116 / 100; (4) composition: ten releases at epsilon 0.1, adversary log-likelihood ratio max 1.0000 (bound 1.0), mean 0.0481, 99th percentile 0.8000 over 100,000 trials; (5) the race (MAE one count / MAE fifty counts under one budget / attacker success over 100,000 trials): Laplace epsilon 1: 1.00 / 50.1 / 0.698 (ceiling 0.731, exact best test 0.697); Laplace epsilon 0.1: 10.00 / - / 0.526; Gaussian (1, 1e-5): 3.86 / 27.3 / 0.544; randomized response epsilon 1 local: 24.4 / - / 0.731 per person; uncalibrated noise std 0.3: 0.24 / - / 0.952; exact release: 0 / 0 / 1.000. Honest: the median's global sensitivity (100) dwarfs its local change (0.116), so the Laplace scale is useless for it; the Gaussian wins the fifty-count batch; author correction recorded (the draft expected Laplace to win the batch too). Cards: self, Gaussian mechanism (algoName Differential privacy), Randomized response, K-anonymity (all resolving). neverUse: exact or uncalibrated release under a differencing attack. Figure: the two Laplace densities one unit apart with the ratio e marked, beside MAE vs epsilon for Laplace and Gaussian with measured points; cite Dwork, McSherry, Nissim, Smith TCC 2006 DOI 10.1007/11681878_14, Dwork and Roth 2014. Viz LaplaceMechanismViz: epsilon 0.5 / 1 / 2 by cycle, 1,500 releases per neighbor per tick for 60 ticks into two histograms with the exact densities, the bin-by-bin ratio against e^epsilon, and a running attacker success against the ceiling; invariant: exact ratio never above e^epsilon and populated-bin ratios within a 30% margin; NODE-VERIFIED 20 cycles x 60 ticks, 0 breaks; stepMs 220, holdTicks rests. Preserved narration: Aoede + Algieba. units.oneLiner: Move to the best neighbor until nothing improves, and when that local optimum is not the goal, throw the state away and climb again from a fresh random start: if one climb succeeds with probability p, the climbs until success are geometric with mean 1/p, so a method that is complete almost never becomes complete almost surely, with no parameter but the budget.
units.description: Hill climbing with random restarts on eight queens and Rastrigin: one climb succeeds 14.3% and 2.7% of the time, the climbs to success (7.83 and 34) match 1/p; at 5,000 evaluations restarts solve eight queens 95.0% against 14.5% for one climb, with tabu 100% and annealing 98%; on Rastrigin at 20,000 evaluations restarts 89% against 3%, annealing and iterated local search 100%; every solution one of the 92.
units.time: about 1/p climbs, each a few hundred evaluations
units.space: one state and its best neighbor
units.plan_row: Hill climbing × Random restarts. Puzzle 178, optimization-or (problemSlug local-search-escape, the atlas problem page carrying "Local optimization"; sibling live lesson annealing-cooling, puzzle 2). Solution hill_climbing_random_restarts.py (12.8s, prints OK): eight queens (attacking-pairs objective, all 92 solutions by exhaustive backtracking as the referee) and two-dimensional Rastrigin (global minimum 0 at the origin, success below 1e-4); steepest-ascent climbing with optional sideways moves, a restart loop, simulated annealing with geometric cooling, tabu search with tenure 7 and aspiration, iterated local search with a two-queen or 1.5-unit kick, a pattern-search climber over eight compass points with a halving step; one currency: objective evaluations. ORACLES: (1) one climb on eight queens over 3,000 starts: success 14.3% (Russell and Norvig about 14%), 4.01 steps on success, 3.06 when stuck; with up to 100 sideways moves 95.4% (about 94%), 18.6 steps on success, 60.4 on failure; every returned solution one of the 92, and all 92 reached across the run; (2) the geometric law: 1/p = 6.99 climbs expected, 7.83 measured over 600 runs (asserted within 15%); Rastrigin 1/p = 38 (p = 2.67% over 20,000 starts, 228 evaluations per climb), 34 measured over 150 runs (within 25%); (3) the queens race at 5,000 evaluations over 200 runs, success / evaluations to success: single climb 14.5% / 227, climb + 100 sideways 95.0% / 946, random restarts 95.0% / 1,520, simulated annealing 98.0% / 2,001, tabu search 100% / 700, iterated local search 89.0% / 1,504; (4) the Rastrigin race at 20,000 evaluations over 100 runs: single climb 3% / 236, restarts 89% / 6,495 (formula 1 - (1 - p)^(budget / climb) predicts 90.6%), annealing 100% / 19,776, iterated local search 100% / 3,709. Honest: tabu search wins the queens race and iterated local search wins Rastrigin outright, sideways moves match restarts on queens at lower cost, and the page says the hero's case is the formula and the absence of parameters; author correction recorded (annealing expected to beat restarts on queens at equal budget, and the rivals' outright wins not expected). Cards: self, Simulated annealing (live lesson badge), Tabu search, Iterated local search (all algoName). neverUse: one greedy climb on a landscape full of local optima. Figure: the geometric success curves for p = 0.143 and 0.0267 with the measured means marked, beside success bars for six methods on both problems; cite Russell and Norvig AIMA section 4.1, Johnson, Papadimitriou, and Yannakakis JCSS 1988 DOI 10.1016/0022-0000(88)90046-3, Selman, Levesque, and Mitchell AAAI 1992. Viz HillClimbingViz: eight queens, one steepest-ascent step per tick, attacking pairs drawn, a stuck climb restarting from a random board (flashed red), climbs counted against 1/p with P(solved within k climbs) on screen, the conflict recount checked every tick and the final board checked against the 92 solutions enumerated at load; NODE-VERIFIED 20 cycles (21.4 ticks per cycle, max 73), 0 breaks; stepMs 550, holdTicks rests. Preserved narration: Aoede + Algieba. units.oneLiner: Center a Gaussian bump of width h on every observation and average them, and set h by the one-line rule 0.9 min(s, IQR/1.34) n^(-1/5), the bandwidth that is optimal for Gaussian data with a robust scale: nearly the oracle on one cloud of points, and a blur on two, because the scale it measures is then the gap between the modes.
units.description: Kernel density estimation with Silverman's bandwidth against the exact integrated squared error of three known densities (n = 300): within 1.00x of the oracle on the Gaussian and 1.10x on the skewed density, but 5.01x on separated modes (h 0.453 against 0.227) where cross-validation reaches 1.03x; histograms 1.97x to 9.14x; the bandwidth shrinks as n^-0.167 and the error as n^-0.690.
units.time: O(n) per evaluation point; one bandwidth from s and IQR
units.baseline: Histogram with Freedman-Diaconis or Sturges bins
units.plan_row: Kernel density estimation × Silverman bandwidth. Puzzle 179, probabilistic (problemSlug density-estimation, the atlas problem page carrying "Density estimation"; sibling live lesson gaussian-mixture-expectation-maximization, puzzle 110). Solution kernel_density_estimation_silverman_bandwidth.py (1.9s, prints OK): three Marron-Wand Gaussian-mixture densities (Gaussian; skewed unimodal #2; separated bimodal #7), a Sample class with precomputed pairwise distances giving the EXACT integrated squared error of a Gaussian KDE at any bandwidth (the three Gaussian-convolution terms in closed form), Silverman's rule, Scott's rule, least-squares cross-validation (Rudemo/Bowman), the oracle bandwidth by a 30-point log grid, exact histogram ISE for Freedman-Diaconis and Sturges bins via the Gaussian CDF, and a nonnegativity and unit-mass check on a wide grid. ORACLES (n = 300): Gaussian (sd 1.03, IQR 1.43): h oracle 0.297, Silverman 0.296, Scott 0.348, LSCV 0.389; ISE multiples Silverman 1.00x, Scott 1.04x, LSCV 1.12x, histogram FD 1.97x (13 bins), Sturges 2.35x (10), h 0.03 7.3x, h 1.5 11.5x; oracle ISE 0.0047. Skewed unimodal (sd 0.83, IQR 1.01): oracle 0.260, Silverman 0.217, Scott 0.282, LSCV 0.198; 1.10x, 1.11x, 1.27x, FD 3.75x (19), Sturges 9.14x (10), 17.6x, 78.8x; oracle 0.0015. Separated bimodal (sd 1.57, IQR 2.97): oracle 0.227, Silverman 0.453, Scott 0.533, LSCV 0.198; 5.01x, 7.82x, 1.03x, FD 7.83x (7), Sturges 4.92x (10), 8.5x, 36.6x; oracle 0.0033. Rates on the Gaussian, twelve samples per n: n 50 / 100 / 200 / 400 / 800: h 0.366 / 0.340 / 0.302 / 0.264 / 0.233, ISE 0.0070 / 0.0080 / 0.0040 / 0.0026 / 0.0011; log-log slopes bandwidth -0.167 (theory -0.200), ISE -0.690 (theory -0.800). Honest: the rule loses to a ten-bin histogram on the separated modes; cross-validation loses to the rule on the Gaussian; three author corrections recorded (cross-validation expected to win everywhere; the KDE expected to beat histograms everywhere; the bandwidth slope sits above -1/5 because the robust scale is biased low at small n). Cards: self, Leave-one-out cross-validation, Gaussian mixture model (live lesson badge), Mean shift (all algoName). neverUse: the rule of thumb on data with separated modes. Figure: the bimodal truth with KDEs at h 0.227 / 0.453 / 0.03 beside the exact ISE-vs-h U with the rule, oracle, and LSCV marked; cite Silverman 1986 3.4.2, Rosenblatt 1956, Parzen 1962 DOI 10.1214/aoms/1177704472, Marron and Wand 1992. Viz KdeViz: a seeded 120-point sample from one of the three densities (by cycle), the bandwidth swept up a 30-step log ladder one step per tick, the estimate drawn against the truth, the ISE U forming on a log-log panel with Silverman's h marked; mass-to-one and ISE nonnegativity checked every tick; NODE-VERIFIED 20 cycles x 30 ticks, 0 breaks; opening seed 20261013 chosen by a scan (Gaussian 1.02x, skewed 1.02x, bimodal 2.72x on the first three cycles) and disclosed; stepMs 320, holdTicks rests. Preserved narration: Aoede + Algieba.
